description: Given two n x n binary matrices mat and target, return true if it is possible to rotate mat by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees to equal target.
examples:
Input: mat = [[0,1],[1,0]], target = [[1,0],[0,1]]
Output: true
Explanation: Rotating mat 90 degrees clockwise gives target.
intuition: There are only 4 possible rotations (0, 90, 180, 270 degrees). Simply rotate the matrix and compare with the target at each step. The rotation formula maps (i,j) to (j, n-1-i) for a 90-degree clockwise turn.
approach: Rotate the matrix 90 degrees at a time (up to 4 times) and check if it matches target at each step. A 90-degree clockwise rotation maps (i,j) to (j, n-1-i).
explanation:
1. Check if the current matrix equals target.
2. Rotate 90 degrees clockwise: new[i][j] = old[n-1-j][i].
3. Repeat up to 4 times (0, 90, 180, 270 degrees).
4. If any rotation matches, return True.
5. After 4 rotations we are back to the original, so return False.
hints: There are only 4 possible rotations to check.
Apply the rotation and compare with target each time.
